references.text: Jesus quotes and comments on this law regarding divorce certificates in the Sermon on the Mount, where he emphasizes that whoever divorces his wife for any reason other than sexual immorality makes her commit adultery.

The Pharisees ask Jesus if it is lawful to divorce one's wife for any reason, directly referencing Moses' provision concerning divorce certificates. Jesus explains that this was a concession due to the hardness of their hearts.

Jesus is asked about divorce and refers to Moses' law on divorce certificates, but explains that this was given because of the people's hard hearts, and that God's original plan was lifelong faithfulness in marriage.
Priests were not allowed to marry a divorced woman, which presupposes the existence of divorce practices as described in Deuteronomy.
A priest's daughter who became a widow or was divorced could return to her father's house, confirming that divorce was an accepted practice.
The Lord asks for the certificate of divorce he is said to have given to Israel's mother, clearly referring to the divorce procedure in Deuteronomy.
Jeremiah uses the metaphor of a divorce certificate regarding God's relationship with Israel and Judah, where Israel received her certificate of divorce due to unfaithfulness.
Malachi condemns faithlessness toward one's wife from youth and says that the Lord hates divorce, highlighting the tension between the permitted practice and God's ideal.
